exposure: Mode of birth for the second child (spontaneous vaginal birth, instrumental vaginal birth, repeat caesarean section, emergency repeat caesarean section)
cohort: A cohort of 94,498 children born as a second child in Sweden between 1999-2015 to women who had a caesarean section in their first pregnancy.
finding: All repeat caesarean sections were associated with increased risks for developmental problems, asthma, allergy, and hospital stay, and emergency repeat caesarean section was linked to an increased risk of death within 5 years, compared to spontaneous vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Repeat caesarean section was related to increased risks for developmental problems, asthma, allergy, and hospital stay, while emergency repeat caesarean section was associated with an increased risk of death within 5 years, with spontaneous vaginal birth showing no increased risk for developmental problems, asthma, or allergy.
